newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP Newcastle workers vote for 24 hr strike.
newsitem.headline: BHP Newcastle workers vote for 24 hr strike.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's (BHP) 3,000 Newcastle workers voted to strike for 24 hours starting immediately in protest against BHP's decision to shut down steel-making at Newcastle by 1999, a union official said on Friday.
"Of the 3,000, only four people voted against the strike," the Australian Workers Union's (AWU) Newcastle Secretary Maurie Rudd told Reuters.
Rudd said the AWU would take a plan to the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU) next week for a national strike of BHP workers.
BHP announced earlier this week a wide-ranging restructure of its steel division, including the closure of its Newcastle steel-making operations and the associated laying off of 2,500 workers.
Newcastle's rod and bar mills would be retained and developed into the centre for BHP's rod, bar and wire business.
Rudd said earlier this week the ACTU might also look at organising a ban on BHP exports, bringing in other non-BHP unions to implement the ban.
Rudd said, however, an export ban was not being immediately considered.
"We haven't gone that far yet," he said.
